definitions.explanation: Having a close biological or taxonomic relationship, such as species within the same genus or family. Primarily used in biology and natural science contexts.
Having a close familial or blood relationship. Used in formal or literary contexts to describe family ties.

examples.japanese: オオカミは{犬|いぬ}の{近縁|きんえん}{種|しゅ}だ。
examples.english: Wolves are a species closely related to dogs.

examples.japanese: この{植物|しょくぶつ}はバラ{科|か}の{近縁|きんえん}{種|しゅ}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: This plant is classified as a species closely related to the rose family.

examples.japanese: DNA{解析|かいせき}により、これまで{別|べつ}の{仲間|なかま}だと{思|おも}われていた{生物|せいぶつ}が{実|じつ}は{近縁|きんえん}であることが{分|わ}かった。
examples.english: DNA analysis revealed that organisms previously thought to belong to different groups are actually closely related.

examples.japanese: {近縁|きんえん}の{者|もの}が{集|あつ}まった。
{近縁|きんえん}の{親族|しんぞく}にのみ{知|し}らせた。
{近縁|きんえん}の{間柄|あいだがら}であっても、{長年|ながねん}{会|あ}っていないと{疎遠|そえん}になることがある。
examples.english: Even close relatives can drift apart if they haven't seen each other for many years.

notes:
USAGE:
{近縁|きんえん} is composed of {近|きん} (close) and {縁|えん} (relation, connection). The biological sense (sense 1) is by far the more common usage in modern Japanese.

Note: Do not confuse with {禁煙|きんえん} (no smoking), which has the same reading but completely different kanji and meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {近縁|きんえん}{種|しゅ} (closely related species)
- {近縁|きんえん}の{生物|せいぶつ} (closely related organisms)
- {近縁|きんえん}{関係|かんけい} (close taxonomic relationship)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {類縁|るいえん} — taxonomic affinity (more technical)
- {親戚|しんせき} — relatives (everyday word for family relations)
